meta_desc_naze: Our own analysis of five problems in the school reorganization plan for eastern Komaki (Shinooka), using “why-why analysis” to find root causes, challenges and solutions (not the city’s view).
meta_title_naze: Why-Why Analysis – Komaki East School Reorganization Navi
naze_a1_c1: 【Fact】The city’s appropriate size is a standard on the number of classes—12 to 24 per school—and the city added to the plan that this means the number of classes, not the number of pupils per class (New School Development Plan).
naze_a1_c2: 🔎 A class-count standard measures whether a school is big enough, not whether learning has improved. There was no step in the planning process to decide the latter.
naze_a1_c3: 【Fact】The city acknowledges that small schools can pay close attention to each child, while listing problems such as no class reshuffling and fewer chances to take on roles (the city’s responses to public comments).
naze_a1_h: Educational quality is not the plan’s first aim<small>教育の質が、計画の第一の目的になっていない</small>
naze_a1_o1: 【Fact】Based on its enrollment projections, the city said there was “no time to wait” and decided to carry out Phase 1 in FY2027, the earliest possible year (the city’s responses to public comments).
naze_a1_o2: 【Fact】The new schools’ educational goals and curriculum have been discussed since July 2025—after the reorganization was decided—by the school reorganization preparatory research committee (Shinooka school reorganization newsletter).
naze_a1_o3: 🔎 Because the work was planned backwards from the deadline, “how many schools” was decided first, and “what to improve” was left for the new schools.
naze_a1_q: 🔎 The plan is built around the number and size of schools. It sets no goals for how learning and growth will improve, and no yardstick to check it. The strengths of small schools are acknowledged but not used in the decision.
naze_a1_r: The plan’s aim was framed as “meeting the size standard,” not “raising educational quality,” and there was no system to hold a yardstick for quality.
naze_a1_t: Educational quality is not the plan’s first aim
naze_a2_c1: 【Fact】School reorganization belongs to the Board of Education, eastern town planning and land use to the Urban Policy Department, child-rearing to the Children’s Future Department, and business location to the Regional Revitalization and Sales Department.
naze_a2_c2: 【Fact】The Eastern Area Development Vision measures results by the share of working-age people; even the November 2026 interim review (draft) has no indicator counting children (Eastern Area Development Council materials).
naze_a2_c3: 🔎 With no department aiming at the number of children, a plan that adapts to “expected decline” exists, but it is never compared, in the same place, with measures that could change the decline.
naze_a2_h: The projection’s assumptions are not shown, and raising the number of children is outside the plan<small>推計の前提が示されず、子どもを増やす取組が計画の外にある</small>
naze_a2_o1: 【Fact】The city explains that because it knows how many children are aged 0–5, it can project enrollment for the next six years quite accurately (the city’s responses to public comments).
naze_a2_o2: 🔎 Numbers six years ahead are almost fixed by children already born. So the projection shows “what happens if current trends continue,” and leaves out what would happen if housing or moving-in changed.
naze_a2_o3: 【Fact】In the Shinooka district, people aged 19 and under are fewer than half of 20 years ago, and people 65 and over are about 2.5 times as many. Meanwhile, the number of workers in the eastern area rose from 12,388 in 2009 to 20,671 in 2014 (Eastern Area Development Vision).
naze_a2_q: 🔎 The assumptions behind the projection that “by 2033 every elementary school and Shinooka JHS will have one class per grade” (births, moves in and out, housing supply) are not shown, and efforts to raise the number of children are placed outside the reorganization plan.
naze_a2_r: The number of children was treated as a fixed given, and there was no system to consider it together with the departments that hold the means to change it (housing, transport, jobs).
naze_a2_t: The projection’s assumptions are not shown, and raising the number of children is outside the plan
naze_a3_c1: 【Fact】The city’s appropriate size is 12 to 24 classes per school, reaching above the national standard (12 to 18 classes).
naze_a3_c2: 🔎 If Phase 1 is done “to match the size standard,” then when schools fall below it again, the same reasoning will justify the next merger.
naze_a3_c3: 【Fact】The national guide revised in August 2026 calls both for careful, dialogue-based discussion and for a timeline that does not postpone conclusions.
naze_a3_h: There is no standard for deciding on Phase 2<small>第2期に進む判断の基準が無い</small>
naze_a3_o1: 【Fact】Phase 2 is to be considered if enrollment falls further after Phase 1, with the decision based on how Phase 1 goes (New School Development Plan).
naze_a3_o2: 【Fact】After the public comments, the city changed its wording on integrated education and Phase 2 from “will introduce” to “will move toward considering introduction.”
naze_a3_o3: 🔎 The wording softened, but “at what number” and “based on what” remain undecided. If numbers simply keep falling without a standard, Phase 2 will happen by drift rather than as the result of a review.
naze_a3_q: 🔎 Phase 2 (one elementary and one junior high school, with integrated 9-year education) is to be considered “if numbers fall further,” but neither that level nor a yardstick for the effects of Phase 1 has been shown.
naze_a3_r: Phase 2 is tied only to the number of children, and the plan contains no system for measuring the results of Phase 1 before deciding.
naze_a3_t: There is no standard for deciding on Phase 2
naze_a4_c1: 【Fact】The maximum class size is 35, and a grade is split into more classes when it goes above that. In the city council, the city said it needs class sizes of “around 21 to 25 pupils that allow class reshuffling.”
naze_a4_c2: 🔎 With a cap of 35, a class can have just over 20 pupils in one grade and be full in another. No step was taken to show and check the pupils and classes per grade after the merger before deciding the closures.
naze_a4_c3: 🔎 Classes, staff, commuting and buildings were each handled by different sections at different times, and there was no place to show the new schools as one whole picture.
naze_a4_h: The shape of the merged schools came after the closure decision<small>統合後の学校の姿が、閉校の決定より後回しになっている</small>
naze_a4_o1: 【Fact】Applications for the school bus were accepted from August 30 to September 30, 2026, while the bus usage guidelines were only announced as “to be handed out at briefings.”
naze_a4_o2: 【Fact】The use of the closing schools is “to be considered,” and the city has indicated it will basically keep the gyms and grounds as community bases while, as a rule, demolishing the school buildings (the city’s responses to public comments).
naze_a4_o3: 🔎 Because the earliest schedule was fixed first, details came in the order of “we will tell you when decided,” and parents had to apply and prepare on the basis of things not yet decided.
naze_a4_q: 🔎 The closure dates were fixed first, but class sizes, staffing and nurse’s offices, commuting rules and the future use of the closed buildings were not shown together at the same time.
naze_a4_r: The schedule was fixed first, with no procedure for presenting the full picture of the new schools (classes, staff, commuting, buildings) before deciding.
naze_a4_t: The shape of the merged schools came after the closure decision
naze_a5_c1: 【Fact】Responsibility is split among the Board of Education, the Urban Policy Department, the Children’s Future Department, the Regional Revitalization and Sales Department and others; overall coordination is handled by the Mayor’s Office (Secretarial and Policy Division). Budgets and ordinances are voted on by the city council.
naze_a5_c2: 🔎 Schools are handled by the Board of Education and the town by other departments, so residents cannot see any place to discuss “the community after the schools close” as a whole.
naze_a5_c3: 【Fact】The national guide revised in August 2026 newly added “careful, dialogue-based discussion” and calls for review together with town planning, including the mayor’s departments (“integration”).
naze_a5_h: Residents cannot see where they can change the decision<small>決め方の中に、住民が変えられる余地が見えない</small>
naze_a5_o1: 【Fact】The city says it began work on the plan in FY2023, explained it at town meetings in FY2024, and in FY2025 at the “thinking about our schools” group, parent exchange meetings and residents’ briefings (the city’s responses to public comments).
naze_a5_o2: 【Fact】The public comment period drew 142 comments from 55 people; the most common topic headings were “timing of Phase 1,” “explanation to the community” and “need for reorganization.” What changed in response were added explanations, school bus safety measures, exchanges between schools, and the wording on Phase 2.
naze_a5_o3: 🔎 The timing—the most common topic—did not change. Unless “what can and cannot be changed” is shown before opinions are invited, those who spoke up are left feeling they were not heard.
naze_a5_q: 🔎 There have been many briefings and calls for comments, but it was never shown in advance what residents’ opinions could change and how far, and no single contact point is visible that takes in the whole picture across departments.
naze_a5_r: Calls for comments were designed as a place for “explanation and notice,” with no system to show in advance what opinions could change and how decisions would be judged, and no contact point across departments.
naze_a5_t: Residents cannot see where they can change the decision
naze_h1: Digging into the Plan with Why-Why Analysis
naze_iss_1: Reset the aim of reorganization to educational quality, and decide goals for academic ability, personal growth and health, with yardsticks to check them.
naze_iss_2: Make it possible to decide on Phase 2 by the results of Phase 1, not only by the number of children.
naze_iss_3: Treat the number of children as something that can change, and set a goal for it together with the departments in charge of housing, transport and jobs.
naze_iss_4: Show, school by school, what the merged schools will look like (pupils and classes per grade, teachers and nurse’s office, commuting) and what will happen to closed buildings.
naze_iss_5: Show in advance what residents’ opinions can change, and have a place that takes them in across departments.
naze_iss_lead: 🔎 Seen from the root cause, five challenges lie ahead. All of them can still be taken up after Phase 1 (April 2027).
naze_list_lead: We start from these five problems in the plan itself.
naze_m_h: What Is Why-Why Analysis?<small>なぜなぜ分析とは</small>
naze_m_p1: Why-why analysis asks “why?” about a visible problem, then asks “why?” again about the answer, and repeats this until it reaches the underlying cause (the root cause). It is widely used in manufacturing. Five rounds is only a guide; you stop when you reach the root cause.
naze_m_p2: Following the approach of a book on how the method is practiced in Denso’s factories, this page keeps three rules.
naze_m_r1: Dig along two paths: “why did it happen?” (causes of the problem) and “why wasn’t it prevented?” (causes in the system) are traced separately.
naze_m_r2: Look at systems, not people: we do not blame anyone; we look for gaps in how decisions and procedures were set up.
naze_m_r3: Check each step: every answer is marked either 【Fact】 (from public records, with sources) or 🔎 (this site’s view).
naze_m_src: Source: “Denso kara Mananda Hontō no ‘Naze-naze Bunseki’” (Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun, 2017). It is cited only to explain the method; neither the book nor Denso analyzed this plan.
naze_p: Starting from five problems in the Shinooka school reorganization plan itself, we keep asking “why?” to find the root causes and the challenges and solutions ahead. This is this site’s own analysis, not the city’s view.
naze_root_core: 🔎 The number of children was accepted as a fixed given, and the plan’s aim became fitting the number of schools to it. As a result, no system was built into the plan for goals and yardsticks of educational quality, standards for the next step, review together with town planning, or the range residents could change.
naze_root_h: The Root Cause All Five Paths Reach<small>5つの道が行き着く真因</small>
naze_root_p: 🔎 When the root causes of the five analyses are put side by side, they reach the same root.
naze_s1_h: Decide yardsticks for learning first, and report every year
naze_s1_p: Publish goals for academic ability, personal growth and health, check them every year at the Phase 1 schools, and report to residents. More: publishing yardsticks first →
naze_s2_h: Set Phase 2 standards by Phase 1 results, and show them in advance
naze_s2_p: Before considering Phase 2, publish standards that look at learning yardsticks and changes in the community, not only “below how many pupils.” Compare ways of keeping small schools—such as special small-school admission—by the same yardsticks.
naze_s3_h: Publish the projection’s assumptions and a target for the number of children
naze_s3_p: Show the assumptions behind the projection, and make “the number of children in the east” some department’s goal. More: assumptions and targets → Make it a department’s goal →
naze_s4_h: Bring the Board of Education and the mayor’s departments to the same table
naze_s4_p: Those in charge of housing, transport and jobs and those in charge of schools discuss the future of the east together. More: one table →
naze_s5_h: Show the merged schools and the closed buildings school by school
naze_s5_p: Lay out pupils and classes per grade, teachers and nurse’s office, and the use of buildings for each school, and add teachers during the transition years. More: extra teachers → School buildings as child-rearing bases →
naze_s6_h: Show what can change before inviting opinions
naze_s6_p: Before calling for comments, show “what can and cannot be changed” and how decisions will be judged, and afterward report, topic by topic, what changed.

rev_s9_lead: These are the divisions in charge of the matters raised on this page. The surest way to test our review is to ask the responsible division directly. Every entry is copied from what the city or the prefecture publishes (as of September 2026).
rev_s9_note: The department names are left in Japanese: that is what you will need to show at the counter or read out on the phone. The main switchboards are 0568-72-2101 for Komaki City Hall and 052-961-2111 for the Aichi Prefectural Government. Names and numbers can change when the offices are reorganized. National divisions are listed on Nationwide Trends. This site has no connection with any of these offices, and you do not need to mention it when you contact them.
